title: Delegate Pricing to Algorithms: When Slow and Steady Wins the Race
abstract: arXiv:2610.11675v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the strategic design of learning algorithms in a canonical continuous-time pricing game. We introduce a meta-game in which firms select learning rates for a gradient dynamic, evaluating payoffs as the discounted sum of profits accrued along the entire learning path. We uncover a fundamental dichotomy driven by stage-game incentives: if the stage game exhibits strategic substitutability, firms unambiguously prefer the fastest possible algorithms to rapidly exploit a gradually adjusting opponent. Under strategic complementarity, however, an excessively fast algorithm accelerates the rival's competitive response, destroying transitional profit margins. Even though the competitive price is a strictly dominant action in the underlying stage game, we prove that firms optimally design sluggish algorithms, extracting surplus during a prolonged convergence to the competitive equilibrium.

translated_title: 将定价委托给算法：当慢而稳赢得比赛时
translated_abstract: 我们研究了标准的连续时间定价博弈中学习算法的战略设计。我们引入了一个元博弈，其中企业为梯度动态选择学习率，并将收益评估为沿整个学习路径累积利润的贴现总和。我们揭示了一个由阶段博弈激励驱动的基本二分法：如果阶段博弈表现出战略替代性，企业会明确偏好最快的算法，以迅速利用逐渐调整的对手。然而，在战略互补性下，过快的算法会加速竞争对手的竞争反应，从而破坏过渡期的利润空间。尽管竞争价格在底层阶段博弈中是严格占优行动，我们证明企业会最优地设计迟缓的算法，在向竞争均衡的漫长收敛过程中提取剩余。
tldr: 该论文发现在战略互补性的算法定价博弈中，即使竞争价格是占优策略，企业仍会理性地选择故意“迟缓”的学习算法，以在向竞争均衡漫长收敛的过程中维持并榨取过渡期利润。
en_tdlr: In algorithmic pricing games with strategic complementarity, firms rationally design deliberately slow learning algorithms—even though the competitive price is strictly dominant—to extract surplus during prolonged convergence to competitive equilibrium.
